images.title: Units and tenths together
images.purpose: Show that 3 units and 4 tenths is the same length as 34 tenths, using ten tenths per unit.
images.composition: Four strips in one row across the frame with white space around; the three full strips are teal and the last strip is partly amber.
exact_structure: Four horizontal strips side by side in one row, each strip a rectangle split into 10 equal cells (40 cells drawn in all).
Strips 1, 2 and 3 are fully teal (#0072B2), 10 cells each, 30 teal cells; a bracket under them is labelled 3 units.
Strip 4 has 4 amber (#E69F00) cells on the left and 6 empty white cells; a bracket under the amber cells is labelled 4 tenths.
A small grey (#6B7280) note above strip 1 reads 10 tenths = 1 unit.
Below the row, centred: 3 4/10 = 34/10 in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box.
rejection: the teal cell count is not 30 or the amber cell count is not 4
a strip split into other than 10 cells
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 3 units and 4 tenths make 34 tenths because each unit is 10 tenths.
images.description: Three full strips of ten teal cells and a fourth strip with four amber cells, showing 3 4/10 equals 34/10.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count 30 teal cells and 4 amber cells to get 34 tenths.

image_decisions.why: The strips make the link between mixed form and count of tenths visible by counting cells.
